เอกสารขอบเขตเมืองเก่าของ ONEP ระบุแนวเขต: ONEP's old-town boundary document places the boundary through Tao Ming School, and the Sirindhorn Anthropology Centre's community database classifies the building as important evidence of the old town. อาคารตั้งอยู่บนถนนศรีตะกั่วป่าในย่านเมือ: The building stands on Thanon Si Takua Pa in the old town and is still used as a destination in tourism materials from the municipality, the Tourism Authority of Thailand, and old-town activities such as the cultural street event held in the Thanon Si Takua Pa area. เอกสารที่เปิดอ่านได้ยังไม่ระบุปีเริ่มสร้: The accessible documents do not identify the park's construction date, builder, or first project. The park's origins can therefore be described only as far as the evidence allows. It should not be directly linked to the tin-mining era or maritime trade, as no documents confirm such continuity.
บริบทของพื้นที่คือเมืองตะกั่วป่าในเขตเมื: The area is Takuapa town's old-town district, with a history of settlement and trade across many periods, including Chinese communities and a mining economy. Contemporary documents verify Thung Phra Pho's role as a public open space for town activities, not as a mining building or an archaeological site with a clearly documented builder.
Southern Thailand Local Database, Prince of Songkla University
ปี 2556 สวนถูกระบุชื่อไว้ในประกาศควบคุมอ: In 2013 (B.E. 2556), the park was named in the building-control announcement for Takuapa Old Town. This means it lies within an old-town landscape where the state regulates construction, but the announcement does not give the park's construction date or original design.
เอกสารแผนงานเทศบาลช่วงปีงบประมาณ 2565 ระ: Municipal planning documents for fiscal year 2022 (B.E. 2565) list a project to install an electrical control cabinet in the park, with a budget of 460,000 baht. They also list dredging the Thung Phra Pho water-supply canal and building a pier on the Takuapa Canal (Thung Phra Pho). This reflects the park's links to the town's water management and infrastructure. A 2013 (B.E. 2556) news report also recorded Thung Phra Pho as a site for installing a water pump during flooding.
เอกสารโครงการเมืองเก่าระบุการจัดลอยกระทง: Old-town project documents record Loy Krathong activities here on the full moon of the twelfth lunar month, including krathong contests, performances, and folk games. The evidence found does not yet verify impacts from the 2004 tsunami (B.E. 2547), abandonment, a change of ownership, or separate registration of the park as an archaeological site.
ข้อมูลแผนที่ปัจจุบันระบุทุ่งพระโพธิ์เป็น: Current map data identifies Thung Phra Pho as a public park in Talat Yai Subdistrict, near Wat Na Muang, Fire Station 2, and the old city wall. It therefore still serves as open space in the old town, but no official announcement confirming opening hours, admission fees, or site-specific facilities was found.
การใช้งานที่ยืนยันได้ในปี 2569 คือโรงเรี: A verified use in 2026 (B.E. 2569) was Takuapa Khirikhate School's Takuapa Walk Rally on 8 March 2026 (B.E. 2569), held at Thung Phra Pho Public Park and in the old town. This reflects the park's use for outdoor learning, health promotion, and sharing local culture.
เอกสารเทศบาลยังยืนยันภาพการใช้งานเพื่อสุ: Municipal documents also confirm health and child-oriented uses, such as a health garden and playground, while old-town documents identify Loy Krathong as an annual activity. However, no recent physical-condition report, long-term restoration project, or caretaker announcement more detailed than the park's municipal ownership has been found.

ประมาณ 200 ปีก่อน; จดทะเบียนวัด พ.ศ. 243: Around 200 years ago; temple registered in 1893 (B.E. 2436)
หลักฐานของสำนักงานนโยบายและแผนทรัพยากรธร: Evidence from the Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning (ONEP) states that Wat Khiri Khet began as a retreat for forest-dwelling monks, used for religious practice, and was around 200 years old when the database was compiled. A more exact construction year should therefore not be asserted. The local name Wat Lum reflects the temple's low-lying terrain in the Old Market area.
แหล่งข้อมูลท้องถิ่นอีกชุดระบุว่าวัดสร้าง: Another set of local sources states that the temple was built or registered on 15 May 1893 (B.E. 2436), and later used the name Wat Phra That Khiri Khet under the Mahanikaya order. It contains an ancient chedi base with a large banyan tree growing on it, and relics of the Buddha that serve as a focus of faith.
ในภาพเมืองตะกั่วป่ายุคเหมืองแร่และการค้า: In the context of Takuapa during the mining and maritime-trade eras, the temple stood near the Old Market and communities where Hokkien Chinese and mining groups settled. However, verifiable sources do not identify a governor or other person as its builder, and no direct evidence connects its builder to any Chinese group. It is therefore safest to describe the temple as a religious site and spiritual anchor for the old-town community, rather than guess at its founder.
พ.ศ. 2462·2563; เหตุการณ์บางช่วงยังไม่ทร: 1919·2020 (B.E. 2462·2563); the year of some events remains unknown
หมุดหมายที่ยืนยันได้คือวัดได้รับพระราชวิ: A verified milestone is that the temple received royal consecration of its monastic boundary on 25 August 1919 (B.E. 2462). This shows that it had developed from its original place of religious practice into a temple with a clear status in the monastic order. The community continues to call it Wat Lum or Wat Talat Tai.
